strengths: Strong opening hook with specific project story (RTF extraction) that immediately establishes domain credibility
Honest acknowledgment of React gap—rare and refreshing, shows self-awareness
Healthcare/regulatory focus directly relevant to Glass Health's clinical decision support mission
Kaiser Permanente investment reference shows genuine company research
Cover letter voice feels authentic and personal, not AI-generated
Resume is clean, scannable, with specific technologies and scale metrics (~100→300+ users, tens of thousands of documents)
The consulting → scaled rollout narrative demonstrates ability to take systems from pilot to production
weaknesses: Resume bullets focus on what was built but could include more outcome metrics (accuracy improvements, time saved, cost reductions)
TypeScript/React depth unclear—skills list shows it but no bullets demonstrate it
Consulting background may raise questions about ownership vs. advisory experience for a founding role
Could strengthen the 'why founding engineer specifically' angle—what excites about 0→1 vs. scaling existing systems
revision_suggestions: Consider adding 1-2 outcome metrics to resume bullets (e.g., 'reduced retrieval latency by X%', 'improved answer accuracy to Y%')
If any TypeScript/React work exists, even minor, consider a bullet to demonstrate familiarity
In cover letter, one more sentence on why founding-stage specifically (beyond 'shape technical direction') could strengthen the fit narrative
